scope: Independent read-only binding, control-flow, helper-source and offline resolver-fixture review. No publication, timestamp, wallet access, upload, workflow dispatch, Git mutation, or repository edit was performed by this review.

finding_and_remediation.initial_finding: The unmodified inherited template recorded DOI resolver failures but did not block OTS or paid work; its main restriction applied at the paid allowance, not at the whole job. It therefore did not satisfy the requested stronger sequencing gates.
finding_and_remediation.parent_remediation: The parent added the explicit main-only job predicate and a nonzero exit after persisting any unsuccessful exact-record resolver result. No inherited preservation/payment mechanisms were altered.
finding_and_remediation.independent_recheck: The final byte-level diff contains only those two guard changes beyond the authorized ID binding and draft-comment removal. Both are present in the final reviewed hash.

checks.detail: The final actual file is exactly the inherited template with its draft-only first comment removed, six remaining ID placeholders replaced by 23279189, and the two documented guard additions. No inherited OTS, spending, intent, upload, or recovery code changed.

The preserve job explicitly requires github.ref == refs/heads/main. Push is restricted to main and this workflow path; hourly cron is 07 * * * *. The authenticated workflow_dispatch actor allowlist is retained. The pinned checkout selects research/ctd-noise-identifiability-v100-20261010. GITHUB_REF_NAME is not assigned or spoofed. The independent allowance also requires the actual GITHUB_REF_NAME to equal main before any paid path.

Credential-free resolution must return HTTP 200 on zenodo.org with exact /records/23279189 or /record/23279189 landing path. The result is written before a nonzero exit unless RESOLVER_PASS and matches_record is exactly true. Normal later steps, including OTS and paid upload, are therefore blocked on failure. Six wholly offline control-flow fixtures passed; no real URL was requested.

Before lifecycle work, the exact single report and DOI are checked. With the mandatory integer bytes field preserved in targets, validate_config compares report, integer record ID, DOI, version, title, and exact PDF filename/bytes/SHA against the publisher public-readback receipt. The initial stamp and frozen bundle construction fetch the anonymous Zenodo PDF and verify its SHA256 and PDF signature; an existing proof is checked directly against the same frozen digest. A cached PDF is rehashed. Exact configured target and receipt registration must precede installation.

Only ready=true enables the budget/paid sequence. New ready=true requires every exact target proof to pass SHA256 binding plus OTS verify with zero exit and Bitcoin-success output. The proxy requires agreement by Blockstream and mempool for target block hashes and 80-byte headers and locally rehashes each header. Pending calendar or merely embedded Bitcoin attestations are insufficient. A known paid transaction may resume only from the hash-bound frozen bundle whose prior per-target states were BITCOIN_VERIFIED_REMOTE_HEADERS. This is remote-header verification, not local full-node consensus.

The live transaction-post hook derives report@doi keys from the payload and rejects prior paid total plus quoted reward >= 100000000000 winston (0.1 AR). It charges a shared bundle fully to each included paper. Unknown/duplicate/zero paper fees and unresolvable historical publication identities fail closed. A known existing transaction resumes readback without charging a new fee. Single transaction reward <= 0.099999999999 AR, remaining wallet reserve >= 0.25 AR, rolling 30-day spend <= 0.50 AR, and configured payload <= 4 MiB remain enforced. The target branch must retain all genuine relevant spending receipts and the current wallet ledger; this audit does not attest to a live balance or ledger freshness after the audited commit.

The payload SHA-bound intent is committed and pushed to the CTD branch before any new paid uploader call. Failure of that push blocks upload. Existing intent without a transaction ID aborts; changed payload or a transaction without its intent aborts. The uploader with a matching retained transaction ID uses only its readback path and does not call create/sign/post again. A first successful post records its transaction ID immediately, before later balance/readback work. If the runner dies between a possibly accepted post and receipt recovery, the persisted intent prevents a blind retry; manual recovery remains necessary.

For an incomplete batch, artifact upload and state commit both use always(). A resolver failure occurs before the batch done output exists, so done != true still holds and the written resolver receipt/target directory are retained. The commit adds only this batch plus the existing wallet-ledger/status files, uses normal push and bounded fetch/rebase retry, and never force-pushes. Non-main events skip the entire job. Artifact retention is 90 days; durable Git receipt commits provide separate retention.

The real main workflow schedules an attempt hourly at minute 07, serialized by main-write-lock with queue max and cancel-in-progress false. Pending OTS can mature across runs; a known paid transaction can resume readback. Completion requires ARWEAVE_READBACK_PASS and matching bundle/public readback SHA256. A completed batch does not stamp or upload again. Resolver outages, branch/budget failures, uncertain paid intents, runner cancellation, or missing artifacts may defer or require recovery; hourly scheduling is not a guarantee of completion.

YAML parsed successfully using BaseLoader; all four external Actions uses are pinned to full 40-character commit hashes. Python uses requirements-ots.txt with opentimestamps-client==0.7.2; Node uses .node-version 22.22.1 and npm ci. A focused inherited OTS unittest command remains in the actual workflow. The audit did not execute that operational workflow.

installation_preconditions: A successful actual publication receipt with exact public PDF readback must be committed at research/noise-identifiability-bodily-judgments/publication-record.json on the CTD target branch before installing this main workflow.

Bind research/paper-timestamps/2026-10-10-paper26-v100/targets.json using record 23279189, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23279189, exact published filename, integer bytes, and full PDF SHA256 from that receipt; keep the bytes field so the strict validator applies.

The target branch checkout must contain the reviewed compatible helper scripts, pinned dependencies, exact targets/receipt, and truthful up-to-date relevant wallet spending ledger. Do not clear or weaken spending history.

Installing the workflow on main is a live push-trigger operation, not merely documentation registration. This static PASS alone does not establish that publication, DOI resolution, Bitcoin verification, or Arweave readback has occurred.
scope_limits: The preservation bundle contains the released PDF, its OTS proof(s), and preservation manifest; it does not automatically include the full reproducibility ZIP.
Bitcoin verification uses the explicitly declared two-provider remote-header transport, not a locally synchronized consensus node.
No paid action was attempted and no live quote, balance, DOI landing page, Zenodo public byte readback, or GitHub execution result was independently queried by this review.
The final generic iteration log is not a completion receipt; use the durable ARWEAVE_READBACK_PASS state with exact readback hashes.
